scope: QtWebEngine download lifecycle regression in the pinned Linux runtime; no Safari original-source claim or browser-engine migration.

observed_sequence: The real truncated HTTP response creates download ID 6 and the user confirms Save.
A second truncated HTTP request is served; Chromium prints ERROR:check.cc(319) NOTREACHED.
Qt emits downloadRequested again for ID 6 in DownloadRequested state, before any observed DownloadInterrupted notification.
The previous implementation opens a second Save sheet. The test has already confirmed the original request, so the second nested confirmation loop reaches the watchdog.
linux_reproduction.interpretation: The trace proves a duplicate-ID request and second confirmation hang. NOTREACHED did not terminate the process at that point. It does not establish the internal Chromium assertion's exact origin.
environment_limits: Disposable CI chroot uses offscreen/software Qt rendering and disables the Chromium sandbox through its harness.
This run is not evidence of production graphics acceleration or sandbox enforcement.

primary_source_evidence.finding: downloadRequested creates a new wrapper and inserts it into m_ongoingDownloads keyed by info.id; downloadUpdated uses that map. There is a debug Q_ASSERT against duplicate IDs. Destruction removes the lookup and delegates native download removal.
The update method emits stateChanged before publishing byte counts and isFinished. cancel() invokes native cancellation only for DownloadInProgress; other states are changed in the Qt wrapper.

DetermineDownloadTarget invokes the profile downloadRequested callback, then accepts or cancels the target callback based on the returned request state. removeDownload delegates to DownloadItem::Remove.

Native observer updates guard against nested updates; cancellation/removal can notify observers. This supports deferring terminal operations outside Qt notification frames, without proving it caused the traced duplicate request.

candidate_behavior: A repeated ID is rejected without a second Save sheet, staging reservation or download-history entry, even if its source view has closed.
The original entry becomes failed with a retry message; partial staging is cleaned and both wrappers are released after the callback frame.
Terminal settlement runs on the next event-loop turn, after Qt has published byte counts and finished state.
Accepted request wrappers are explicitly released with deleteLater so native ownership ends after signal frames.

passed: verify_web_downloads.py: real completed downloads, collision protection, UTF-8 names, active cancellation, real truncated responses, source-tab close, private-window cleanup and pending Save close.
Exact Qt field-order fixture: final byte counts are preserved and cancellation does not reenter the update frame.
Same-ID retry fixture: no second prompt or entry, original failure, no published partial file and empty staging.
verify_browser_profiles.py: shared regular-window cookies/download ownership, isolated private sessions, real process restart persistence and interactive tab overview.
verify_web_page.py: real local navigation/load, bookmarks, tabs and cleanup.

observed: The real broken-response fixture still reaches Chromium NOTREACHED and emits the duplicate ID 6.
The new duplicate-rejected and duplicate-finalized paths execute, and the test proves a failed entry with no published partial file or remaining staging.
All subsequent download-after-tab-close, shared/private profile and window-close cases pass.
The mandatory page and profile suites also pass, including regular-cookie persistence across a real process restart.

verification.full_linux_build_status: not established by these browser-only checks

remaining_limits: The upstream Chromium NOTREACHED diagnostic remains; the application now handles the resulting duplicate request without hanging. No native Chromium patch is claimed.
Automatic resume of the duplicate request is not implemented. The failed entry directs the user to start a new download.
These tests do not establish native compositor rendering, hardware acceleration, production Chromium sandbox enforcement or Safari visual/animation parity.
